It turns"},{"id":"p4s2","text":" one AI coding agent into a bounded orchestration cohort: configurable AI agent Specialists, an exac"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"t LLM model router, declarative Cohorts and Strategies, structured results, and depth-limited subage"},{"id":"p4s4","text":"nt delegation — without replacing the DSH runtime."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## What is dsh-legion used for?"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"Legion is useful when one AI coding agent should delegate different kinds of work under explicit, re"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"ul when one AI coding agent should delegate different kinds of work under explicit, reusable policy."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- **Route work by task type.** Send extraction or summaries to a fast model and architecture or debu"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"gging to a deeper model.
- **Run independent reviews.** Give a reviewer read-only tools, a separate "},{"id":"p7s3","text":"persona, and a structured `review-v1` result.
- **Build multi-agent workflows.** Define bounded Coho"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"rts and declarative plan/execute/review or research fanout Strategies.
- **Bound workload and risk.*"},{"id":"p7s5","text":"* Limit depth, concurrency, participants, deadlines, output size, tools, and eligible routes. These "},{"id":"p7s6","text":"bounds constrain cost drivers, but Legion does not provide aggregate token or monetary-cost admissio"},{"id":"p7s7","text":"n.
- **Standardize delegation.** Keep semantic Specialist names stable when the underlying model or "},{"id":"p7s8","text":"backend changes.
- **Validate policy before runtime.** Diagnose configuration against explicit provi"},{"id":"p7s9","text":"der capability fixtures.
- **Customize without forking.** Add, replace, disable, or revive Specialis"},{"id":"p7s10","text":"ts, Cohorts, and Strategies through Catalog Layers."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"Legion is for developers and deployment owners who already use DSH and want configurable multi-agent"},{"id":"p8s2","text":" delegation without adopting another scheduler, session store, or agent runtime."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## Capabilities"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"| Capability | What it provides |"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"| Semantic Specialists | Named policies such as `quick`, `deep`, and `review` instead of raw model c"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"hoices in every prompt. |
| Exact model routing | Up to eight ordered provider/model candidates with"},{"id":"p11s3","text":" static context and output-budget constraints. |
| Multiple backends | Use `spawn`, `fork`, `codex`,"},{"id":"p11s4","text":" `claude-code`, or another DSH-registered subagent provider per Specialist. |
| Tool and persona pol"},{"id":"p11s5","text":"icy | Restrict child tools, add Specialist instructions, set depth, and choose foreground/background"},{"id":"p11s6","text":" defaults. |
| Structured results | Versioned `text`, `findings-v1`, and `review-v1` foreground resu"},{"id":"p11s7","text":"lt contracts. |
| Custom Cohorts | Declare bounded Member Slots that reference existing Specialists."},{"id":"p11s8","text":" |
| Declarative Strategies | Compile typed artifact graphs to frozen DSH delegation primitives. |

- A DSH Host `profile`, such as the default `web` composition.
- A configured DSH su"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"bagent provider and the LLM provider/model routes referenced by your Specialists.
- For local develo"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"pment: Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` and pnpm `11.21.0`."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"## Status and limitations"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"The source tree declares version `1.2.0`; canonical current configuration is v3, while published 1.x"},{"id":"p15s2","text":" no-target materialization/export remains v2 for compatibility. Check CHANGELOG.md, the roadmap, and"},{"id":"p15s3","text":" GitHub Releases before selecting or upgrading an install revision."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Known limitations:"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"- Curated Strategies are not automatically model-exposed; deployment owners may opt in with `enableS"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"trategies: true`.
- DSH has no unified recovery owner across provider retries and Route Candidates, "},{"id":"p17s3","text":"so Legion starts only the selected child and never retries or switches models after failure.
- DSH b"},{"id":"p17s4","text":"inds a prepared call to one adapter generation and one dispatch, but Legion's pre-start Route observ"},{"id":"p17s5","text":"ations are point-in-time, best-effort facts rather than an atomic adapter-topology snapshot.
- A Spe"},{"id":"p17s6","text":"cialist cannot override a child's reasoning effort.
- In-process children inherit the parent's named"},{"id":"p17s7","text":" DSH agent preset; no per-child named preset or Specialist-local DSH Skill setup is available across"},{"id":"p17s8","text":" one-shot, continuable, and cold-resume paths. Specialists can still vary model, persona, tools, bac"},{"id":"p17s9","text":"kend, and limits.
- Legion does not inspect live provider health, credentials, authorization, quota,"},{"id":"p17s10","text":" reachability, or latency; Route Plans report those facts as unknown.
- Aggregate token or monetary-"},{"id":"p17s11","text":"cost admission remains a future Host-owned capability; it is unrelated to the observation-only Run R"},{"id":"p17s12","text":"eceipt companion. Current limits cover members, concurrency, deadlines, accepted output, tools, and "},{"id":"p17s13","text":"eligible routes.
- The GUI settings card edits five scalar policies; Specialists, Cohorts, Strategie"},{"id":"p17s14","text":"s, and catalog layers stay in the configuration document.
- DSH now publishes assessed-line client c"},{"id":"p17s15","text":"ontracts, including the `settings.plugin.item` slot declaration, but not its `clientBundle` build pr"},{"id":"p17s16","text":"eset. Legion therefore typechecks against public packages while reproducing the loader artifact form"},{"id":"p17s17","text":"at by hand; a Host format change fails at load time rather than at build time.
